questions.explain: $|\vec{v}| = 5$, so $\hat{v} = (3/5, 4/5) = (0.6, 0.8)$. Dividing by the component sum (7) gives a vector whose length is not 1.

questions.q: The vector $(0.3, 0.4)$ has length $0.5$. What does normalizing it do?
questions.explain: Dividing by a length below 1 makes the arrow longer: $(0.3, 0.4)/0.5 = (0.6, 0.8)$, which has length 1.

questions.q: Why can the zero vector $(0, 0)$ **not** be normalized?
options: It is already a unit vector
Its length is 0, so we would divide by 0
questions.explain: Normalizing means $\vec{v} / |\vec{v}|$; for the zero vector that is division by zero, and there is no direction to keep anyway.

questions.q: The page's 3D default is $(2, 3, 6)$ with length 7. Which statement about its unit vector is true?
options: It points in a different direction but has length 1
It is $(2/7, 3/7, 6/7) \approx (0.29, 0.43, 0.86)$ and points in the same direction
questions.explain: Normalizing divides every component by the length (7): the direction is kept exactly, only the size changes to 1.
